comment: The vectors pinning Prima.HostAPI as it crosses HTTP (Prima.WorkerWire): every call a runner makes and the report a worker service makes, sealed and signed with the keys of tests/fixtures/worker_auth.json, whose values keys repeats (root_hex is the root every other key derives from). Every consumer reproduces each call from its fields: body is the request body Prima.WorkerWire.request_body/2 writes, sealed as body_sealed in the body direction under the attempt seal key with body_iv_hex (Prima.WorkerAuth.seal_call/5); header is the host-call header over body_sealed, the bytes posted, under the attempt call key; answer is the answer written for it, sealed as answer_sealed in the answer direction with answer_iv_hex. Every body and answer carries v, the wire version, as its first member; a body whose v is absent or not version is unknown_version after it is opened and before its op is read, and an answer without it, or at another, is a lost answer. refusals are the plain answers each call may be given instead, with why. pre_body_refusals are headers a listener refuses before it reads a body, at now, for the member at standing, each answered at status with the refusal error names, in the order Prima.WorkerAuth documents: a version token other than v1, a header that does not parse, a timestamp outside window_ms, a MAC that is not the call key's, another generation, another member at the same generation, and a nonce the storage call (never retried) already presented for its attempt within the window. body_refusals are opened bodies posted at the renew route, refused with error. report is a worker service's runner_exited, plain under its dispatch key, answered plain; its cross_member names another member than the verifying one and is refused with error. retry_identity is one admit_child body sent twice, each time sealed and signed afresh under a new timestamp and nonce: the body, and so its child_key, is the same. connection_cases are admit_child calls under one attempt, in order, each answered as CYFR answers it for an attempt whose edge to the reference binds no named account: omitted names no connection and is admitted, its answer holding the child's assignment and in it the child's authority as the host answers it; named names the account Work, which the edge does not bind, and is refused connection_not_granted, setup required, with no default used in its place; reused repeats omitted's child_key naming Work, and is refused invalid_request before anything is answered from that key's child, since a key names one child and the connection it was admitted with. egress_pin_cases are egress_pin calls by name, answered with a Prima.PinnedTarget (id, ip, family, scheme, port, host, expires_at) or refused as Prima.PinnedTarget.refusals/0 names; a redirect names the pin its hop came from as from. egress_policy_cases are egress_pin calls in the order one attempt makes them, under an authority whose egress.domains is domains, each answered as an egress_pin case is; expect names whether the URL's host matches domains (domain_allowed, Prima.Network.domain_allowed?/2) and, for a redirect, whether its URL has the origin of the URL whose pin it names as from (same_origin, Prima.Network.same_origin?/2: scheme, host and effective port). A pin is answered only where both hold; a first request outside domains is denied and a hop to another origin is redirect_credentials. attached_fetch is the one call whose success is no single answer: posted with a Prima.AttachedRequest naming the runner's call_id, it is refused before admission by an ordinary sealed answer, a guest_error whose call_id is the request's (its refusals, each sealed with answer_iv_hex as answer_sealed), and admitted it is answered with frames, so the call carries no answer and the frames are frame_cases. A frame is a 4-byte big-endian length, one kind byte in clear (h head, c chunk, e end, x error) and the sealed value: Prima.MacEnvelope's seal of the plaintext under the attempt seal key, label cyfr-locus/v1/runtime/frame-answer, fields call_id, seq and kind (Prima.WorkerAuth.seal_frame/7). Each case's frames are read in order by a reader for call_id, one frame at a time; sealed_for says what a frame was sealed as (its call_id, seq, kind, iv_hex and plaintext_b64), tampered_from what a changed frame was sealed as before it changed, and expect the frames read (a head's status and headers, a chunk's body_b64, an end, an error's type and message) and the refusal that ends the answer, or null. egress_pin_internal_purposes are egress_pin calls naming a purpose CYFR alone takes (attached), each refused malformed. framing_headers and override_headers are the lowercase names, in order, of the headers a guest request, ordinary or attached, may not set and an attach rule may not name: those that route or frame a request (Prima.Network.framing_headers/0) and those that override its method or target or claim a forwarded origin, a proxy hop or a client address (Prima.Network.override_headers/0); override_prefixes are the lowercase prefixes (Prima.Network.override_prefixes/0) any name starting with which is one of the latter too. An attached request setting one, in any case, is refused invalid_request naming it as spelled. credential_headers are the lowercase names, in order, of the headers that carry a credential (Prima.Network.credential_headers/0): an attached request naming one, in any case, is refused credential_header_refused. A catalyst's ask (question_ask, question_wait): question_ask's body pins ask_no, a positive integer the runner takes once for each call of the guest's ask, and the request's action, summary and operation; question_wait's pins ask_no and max_wait_ms, at most Prima.HostAPI.max_question_wait_ms/0. Each answer is a success: {answer}, {pending: true}, or for question_ask {retry_after_ms}, a positive integer, an answer being "allowed", "denied" or {"none": "unattended" | "invalid" | "unavailable"} (Prima.HostAPI.answer_to_wire/1); each is refused lost for an attempt that is not live. question_cases holds them in the order one attempt asks: request_digests are a request's digest, SHA-256 as lowercase hexadecimal over its action, summary and operation, each prefixed with its UTF-8 byte length as an unsigned 32-bit big-endian integer (Opus.Host.Question.request_digest/3), and cases are calls, each answered as CYFR answers it: opened admits an ask whose question opens; keyed_replay is opened's body under a fresh header, answered the same wait; changed is opened's number with another request, invalid; paced is past its root's allowance and paced_admitted the same body sent again, admitted; unattended and invalid are asks answered at once; and the waits are one that timed out, pending, and one of each final answer.
